title: Simple machines
summary: Learn about levers, pulleys, inclined planes, the wheel and axle, screws, gears, and efficiency.
cards.0.p: A simple machine makes work easier by changing the size, the direction, or the distance of a force. The lever, pulley, inclined plane, wheel and axle, screw, and gear are all simple machines.
cards.0.key: In calculations we assume that pulleys and bars are weightless and that there is no friction.
cards.0.once.soru: What does the pulley at the top of a flagpole do?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.yazi: It changes the direction of the force
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: You pull the rope down to raise the flag.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: A fixed pulley gives no gain in force.
cards.1.h: Gain in force, loss in distance
cards.1.p: Mechanical advantage is the ratio of the load to the effort (W / F). If it is 4, you lift a 400 N load with 100 N, but you pull 4 times as much rope. So there is no gain in work.
cards.1.key: In an ideal machine F·xF = W·xW. What you gain in force you lose in distance.
cards.1.once.soru: A machine lifts a 400 N load with 100 N. How many meters of rope do you pull while the load rises 1 m?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: If you gain 4 times in force, you lose 4 times in distance, because 100·4 = 400·1.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: When the force goes down, the distance goes up, and the work stays the same.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: If the distance got shorter, you would gain work, and that never happens.
cards.2.h: The lever and the balance condition
cards.2.p: A lever is a bar that turns around a pivot (fulcrum). The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the effort is the effort arm, and the distance to the load is the load arm. At balance F·dF = W·dW.
cards.2.key: The advantage of a lever is dF / dW. The arm is not the length of the bar. It is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force.
cards.2.etk.soru: Change the arms: F·d<sub>F</sub> = W·d<sub>W</sub>. What happens as the effort arm gets longer?
cards.3.p: The order of the pivot, the load, and the effort sets the type of lever. On a seesaw the pivot is in the middle. On a wheelbarrow the load is in the middle, and the advantage is greater than 1. With tweezers the effort is in the middle, and the advantage is less than 1.
cards.3.key: Most of the levers in your body (such as the forearm) have the effort in the middle, and they magnify motion.
cards.3.etk.soru: What is in the middle of this lever: the pivot, the load, or the effort?
cards.3.etk.ogeler.1.2: The screw (pivot) is between the handles and the blades.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.2.2: The rivet (pivot) is between the handles and the jaws.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.3.2: The wheel is the pivot, the load is in the middle, and you lift at the end.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.4.2: The nut sits between the hinge and your hand.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.5.2: The top of the cap is the pivot, and the edge being lifted is in the middle.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.6.2: Your fingers press between the hinge and the tips.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.7.2: Your hand squeezes in the middle, and the tips hold the load.
cards.3.etk.ogeler.8.2: The lower hand is the pivot, and the upper hand applies the effort in the middle.
cards.4.p: A fixed pulley is attached to the ceiling and does not move with the load. Its advantage is 1, so F = W. Its benefit is that it changes the direction of the force. You pull the rope down to lift the load.
cards.4.key: A fixed pulley gives no gain in force or in distance. It only changes the direction of the force.
cards.4.once.soru: With a fixed pulley, how many newtons do you pull with to balance a 200 N load?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: A fixed pulley gives no gain in force, so F = W.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: It is the movable pulley that halves the force.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: A fixed pulley does not increase the force. It only changes its direction.
cards.5.p: A movable pulley rises with the load, and two rope strands carry the load. So F = W/2, and the advantage is 2. The price is that to lift the load by h you pull 2h of rope.
cards.5.key: If the pulley weighs w, then F = (W + w)/2. If the rope strands are not parallel, the advantage is less than 2.
cards.5.once.soru: With a weightless movable pulley, how many newtons do you need to lift a 300 N load?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: Two rope strands share the load, and 300 / 2 = 150 N.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: That is true for a fixed pulley.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: A movable pulley halves the force.
cards.6.p: A block and tackle combines fixed and movable pulleys. If n rope strands carry the movable block, then F = W/n. When the load rises by h, you pull n·h of rope.
cards.6.key: When counting n, count only the strands attached to the movable block. If the movable pulleys weigh w, then F = (W + w)/n.
cards.7.p: If you push a load up a sloped surface with no friction, F·L = W·h (L is the length of the ramp, h is the height). The longer the ramp, the smaller the force, but the longer the distance.
cards.7.key: The advantage of an inclined plane is L/h. For the same height, the work W·h does not change.
cards.8.p: A wheel and axle is a large handle and a small cylinder fixed to the same shaft. At balance F·R = W·r, and the advantage is R/r. A door handle, a steering wheel, and a screwdriver work this way.
cards.8.key: A well windlass works the same way. In one turn the effort moves 2πR and the load moves 2πr.
cards.8.once.soru: Why does a thick-handled screwdriver turn a screw more easily than a thin-handled one?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: For a wheel and axle the advantage is R/r. A larger handle gives the same turning effect with less force.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Weight does not make turning easier.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: It is the radius of the handle, not its length, that makes it easier.
cards.9.p: When simple machines are connected, their advantages multiply. A movable pulley (2) combined with a wheel and axle with R = 4r (4) gives an advantage of 8. So an 800 N load is lifted with 100 N.
cards.9.key: While the load rises h, the end of the handle moves 8h. With no friction, the work does not change in a compound system either.
cards.9.once.soru: A pulley with advantage 2 is connected to a wheel and axle with advantage 3. What is the total advantage?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: For machines connected in a chain the advantages multiply, giving 2 · 3.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: Advantages multiply, they do not add.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Advantages do not divide. Each machine reduces the force again.
cards.10.p: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder. The distance between neighboring threads is the pitch (a), and the screw advances by a in one turn. With no friction F·2πR = W·a.
cards.10.key: Here R is the length of the handle. A jack and a vise work this way. A real screw has a lot of friction, which is why it does not turn back by itself.
cards.10.once.soru: How far does a screw advance in one full turn?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: In one turn the screw advances by the distance between two neighboring threads.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: It takes many turns to drive a screw all the way in.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The circumference is the distance the end of the handle moves. It is not how far the screw advances.
cards.11.p: The rims of meshing gears move at the same speed. So the number of turns is inversely proportional to the radius, and n₁·r₁ = n₂·r₂. Meshing gears turn in opposite directions.
cards.11.key: You can use the number of teeth instead of r. An open belt keeps the direction, and a crossed belt reverses it. Gears on the same shaft make the same number of turns.
cards.11.once.soru: A 20-tooth gear meshes with a 10-tooth gear. When the large gear makes 1 turn, how many turns does the small one make?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: 1·20 = n·10: the small gear turns twice as fast.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The small gear makes more turns, not fewer.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: The numbers of teeth are different, so the numbers of turns are different too.
cards.12.p: The pedal shares a shaft with the front gear, and the rear gear shares one with the wheel, and the chain links the two. If the front gear has 48 teeth and the rear gear has 16, the wheel makes 3 turns for each turn of the pedal.
cards.12.key: On a hill you shift to a larger rear gear. The wheel then turns less, and pedaling gets easier. Gears linked by a chain turn in the same direction.
cards.13.p: In a real machine, friction turns part of the work into heat. Efficiency is the useful work divided by the work input, times 100, and it is always below 100%.
cards.13.svg#0: Ramp: W = 600 N, h = 1 m, L = 4 m, F = 200 N
cards.13.svg#6: Without friction F = 150 N would be enough
cards.13.key: If you apply 200 N to raise a 600 N load by 1 m on a 4 m ramp, the efficiency is 600 J / 800 J = 75%.
cards.14.p:
• The advantage is W / F, and there is no gain in work.
• For a lever F·dF = W·dW.
• The advantage is 1 for a fixed pulley, 2 for a movable pulley, and n for a block and tackle.
• F·L = W·h for an inclined plane, F·R = W·r for a wheel and axle, and F·2πR = W·a for a screw.
• For gears n₁·r₁ = n₂·r₂.
quiz.0.q: A 600 N load is lifted with a block and tackle whose movable block is carried by 4 rope strands. If the movable pulleys weigh 40 N in total, what is the smallest force, in N, you must apply to the rope? (no friction)
quiz.0.e: The weight of the pulleys adds to the load, so F = (W + w) / n = (600 + 40) / 4 = 160 N.
quiz.1.q: Put each case in the right group by lever type.
quiz.1.ogeler.0.0: Lifting a rock with a crowbar
quiz.1.e: For a crowbar and a balance the pivot is in the middle. For a paper guillotine and for rising onto your toes the load is in the middle. On your toes, the toes are the pivot and the effort is the muscle at the heel. With a broom and a shovel the upper hand is the pivot, and the lower hand applies the effort in the middle.
quiz.2.q: A 300 N load hangs from one end of a 2 m weightless bar. The pivot is 0.5 m from the load. What is the smallest force, in N, applied perpendicular to the other end that balances the bar?
quiz.2.e: The effort arm is 2 − 0.5 = 1.5 m. Since F·1.5 = 300·0.5, F = 100 N. The advantage is 1.5 / 0.5 = 3.
quiz.3.q: Gears K, L, and M mesh in a row and have radii r, 3r, and 2r. If K makes 6 turns clockwise, what does M do?
quiz.3.e: For gears in contact n·r is constant. Since 6·r = n·2r, n = 3. L turns opposite to K. M turns opposite to L, which is the same direction as K: clockwise.
quiz.3.y.0: The middle gear L reverses the direction twice. So K and M turn in the same direction, not in opposite directions.
quiz.3.y.1: The number of turns is inversely proportional to the radius. If 6·r = n·2r, then n = 3, and the direction is the same as K.
quiz.3.y.3: The number of turns is inversely proportional to the radius. So the larger gear M makes fewer turns than K.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Balance the lever, lift a load with a block and tackle, and change the gear.
A:adimlar.0.metin: A 400 N load is 0.5 m from the pivot. The bar balances when force times distance is equal on both sides of the pivot. Balance the bar with the force you apply 2 m away.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: 400 · 0.5 = 100 · 2 = 200 N·m. The effort arm is 4 times the load arm, so the force is 4 times smaller. That means the advantage is dF / dW = 4.
A:adimlar.1.metin: The order of the pivot (P), the load (W), and the effort (F) sets the type of lever. The item in the middle tells you which arm can be longer.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: With the pivot in the middle, the advantage depends on the lengths of the arms and can also be greater than 1.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: With the load in the middle, the effort arm is always longer than the load arm. So the advantage is greater than 1.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: With the effort in the middle, the effort arm is always shorter than the load arm, and the advantage is less than 1. In return, the tip moves farther.
A:adimlar.2.baslik: Pulleys and the block and tackle
A:adimlar.2.metin: Change the number of rope strands carrying the movable block. Lift the 400 N load with 100 N.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.tamam: 4 rope strands share the load, and 400 / 4 = 100 N. But when the load rises 1 m, you pull 4 m of rope. You gain in force and lose in distance. The work is still 400 J.
A:adimlar.3.metin: You will raise a 600 N crate by 1 m using a ramp. Make the ramp longer and bring the force needed down to 150 N.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 600 · 1 / 4 = 150 N. The ramp is 4 times longer, so the force is 4 times smaller. The work is always 600 J. A machine does not reduce the work, it only makes it easier.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The front gear has 48 teeth. Make the wheel turn 4 times for each turn of the pedal. Choose the rear gear and press play.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: Since 48 / 12 = 4, the wheel makes 4 turns. If the wheel's circumference is 2 m, the bike travels 8 m per pedal turn. The bike is fast, but pedaling gets harder.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A real ramp has friction. Efficiency is the ratio of useful work to work input. Raising a 600 N load by 1 m on a 5 m ramp took a force of 150 N.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: What is the efficiency of this ramp, in percent?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Efficiency cannot exceed 100%. You divided the work input by the useful work. Do the reverse.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The useful work is 600 · 1 = 600 J, and the work input is 150 · 5 = 750 J. The efficiency is 600 / 750 = 80%. The remaining 150 J turned into heat.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: 20% is the part that goes into heat. Efficiency is the ratio of useful work to work input.
A:kapanis.0: Mechanical advantage is W / F. What you gain in force you lose in distance, and in an ideal machine the work does not change.
A:kapanis.1: For a balanced lever F·dF = W·dW. With tweezers the effort is in the middle, and the advantage is less than 1.
A:kapanis.2: The advantage is 1 for a fixed pulley and 2 for a movable pulley. For a block and tackle it equals the number of rope strands (n) carrying the load.
A:kapanis.3: For an inclined plane F·L = W·h. For gears n₁·r₁ = n₂·r₂.
A:kapanis.4: Efficiency is the ratio of useful work to work input, and in a real machine it is below 100%.
